import csv

rows = list(csv.DictReader(open('eu_economic_data.csv')))
for r in rows:
    for k in r:

            r[k] = float(r[k])

BLUE = "#1f4e79"; STEEL = "#2E86AB"; RED = "#C0392B"; GREEN = "#1E8449"
AMBER = "#B9770E"; GREY = "#7F8C8D"; LIGHT = "#F4F6F7"; GRID = "#D5DBDB"

def esc(t): return t.replace("&","&").replace("<","<").replace(">",">")

def svg_open(w, h): return f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{w}" height="{h}" viewBox="0 0 {w} {h}" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif">'
def text(x, y, s, size=13, fill="#2C3E50", anchor="start", weight="normal", style=""):
    return f'<text x="{x}" y="{y}" font-size="{size}" fill="{fill}" text-anchor="{anchor}" font-weight="{weight}" {style}>{esc(s)}</text>'
def rect(x, y, w, h, fill, rx=0, opacity=1):
    return f'<rect x="{x}" y="{y}" width="{w}" height="{h}" fill="{fill}" rx="{rx}" opacity="{opacity}"/>'
def line(x1, y1, x2, y2, stroke, width=1, dash=""):
    d = f' stroke-dasharray="{dash}"' if dash else ""
    return f'<line x1="{x1}" y1="{y1}" x2="{x2}" y2="{y2}" stroke="{stroke}" stroke-width="{width}"{d}/>'
def circle(cx, cy, r, fill, stroke="none", sw=0):
    s = f' stroke="{stroke}" stroke-width="{sw}"' if stroke != "none" else ""
    return f'<circle cx="{cx}" cy="{cy}" r="{r}" fill="{fill}"{s}/>'

def hbar_chart(fname, title, subtitle, items, x_label, xmin, xmax, ref=None, ref_label=None,
               color_pos=GREEN, color_neg=RED, fmt="{:.1f}", unit=""):
    """items: list of (label, value) sorted by value ascending for horizontal bars"""
    W, H = 960, 60 + 52*len(items) + 60
    pad_l, pad_r, pad_t, pad_b = 210, 90, 90, 56
    plot_w = W - pad_l - pad_r
    def X(v): return pad_l + (v - xmin)/(xmax - xmin)*plot_w
    body = [svg_open(W, H),
            text(40, 42, title, 22, BLUE, weight="bold"),
            text(40, 66, subtitle, 14, GREY)]
    # gridlines
    for i in range(5):
        v = xmin + (xmax - xmin)*i/4
        gx = X(v)
        body.append(line(pad_l, pad_t, pad_l, H-pad_b, GRID, 1))
        body.append(text(gx, H-pad_b+18, f"{v:{fmt}}{unit}", 11, GREY, "middle"))
    # reference line
    if ref is not None:
        body.append(line(X(ref), pad_t, X(ref), H-pad_b, RED, 1.5, "6,4"))
        if ref_label: body.append(text(X(ref)+6, pad_t-6, ref_label, 11, RED))
    # bars
    n = len(items)
    bar_h = min(34, (H - pad_t - pad_b - 10)/n - 8)
    for i, (label, v) in enumerate(items):
        y = pad_t + i*(bar_h + 8) + 4
        body.append(text(pad_l-12, y + bar_h/2 + 4, label, 13, "#2C3E50", "end", "bold"))
        color = color_pos if v >= 0 else color_neg
        bw = max(2, (v - xmin)/(xmax - xmin)*plot_w) if v >= 0 else max(2, (xmin - v)/(xmax - xmin)*plot_w)
        if v >= 0:
            body.append(rect(X(0), y, max(2, X(v)-X(0)), bar_h, color, 3))
        else:
            body.append(rect(X(v), y, X(0)-X(v), bar_h, color, 3))
        body.append(text(X(v) + (10 if v >= 0 else -10), y + bar_h/2 + 4, f"{v:+.1f}", 12, "#2C3E50", "start" if v >= 0 else "end", "bold"))
    # zero line
    body.append(line(X(0), pad_t, X(0), H-pad_b, "#2C3E50", 1.2))
    body.append(text(pad_l, H-pad_b+42, x_label, 12, GREY, "middle"))
    body.append('</svg>')
    open(f"charts/{fname}", "w").write("\n".join(body))

def line_chart_dual(fname, title, subtitle):
    """Dual-axis line chart: Inflation vs GDP Growth, EU total 2022-2024"""
    W, H = 960, 520
    pad_l, pad_r, pad_t, pad_b = 80, 70, 90, 70
    plot_w, plot_h = W - pad_l - pad_r, H - pad_t - pad_b
    years = [2022, 2023, 2024]
    infl = [9.2, 6.4, 2.4]; growth = [3.4, 0.4, 0.9]
    def X(y): return pad_l + (y - 2022)/2*plot_w
    def Y1(v): return pad_t + plot_h - (v - 0)/10*plot_h
    def Y2(v): return pad_t + plot_h - (v - (-1))/6*plot_h
    body = [svg_open(W, H),
            text(40, 40, title, 22, BLUE, weight="bold"),
            text(40, 64, subtitle, 14, GREY)]
    # grid + y1 labels (inflation)
    for i in range(6):
        v = i*2; gy = Y1(v)
        body.append(line(pad_l, gy, W-pad_r, gy, GRID, 1))
        body.append(text(pad_l-10, gy+4, f"{v}%", 11, GREY, "end"))
    body.append(text(22, pad_t + plot_h/2, "Inflation (CPI)", 12, RED, "middle", "bold", 'transform="rotate(-90 22 %d)"' % (pad_t+plot_h/2)))
    # y2 labels (growth)
    for i in range(7):
        v = -1 + i
        gy = Y2(v)
        body.append(text(W-pad_r+10, gy+4, f"{v}%", 11, "#2C3E50", "start"))
    body.append(text(W-pad_r+30, pad_t-20, "GDP growth", 12, BLUE, "middle", "bold"))
    # x labels
    for y in years:
        body.append(text(X(y), H-pad_b+24, str(y), 12, "#2C3E50", "middle", "bold"))
    # inflation line (red, right axis mapped to left but scaled)
    pts_i = " ".join(f"{X(y)},{Y1(v)}" for y, v in zip(years, infl))
    pts_g = " ".join(f"{X(y)},{Y2(v)}" for y, v in zip(years, growth))
    body.append(f'<polyline points="{pts_i}" fill="none" stroke="{RED}" stroke-width="3.5"/>')
    body.append(f'<polyline points="{pts_g}" fill="none" stroke="{BLUE}" stroke-width="3.5"/>')
    for y, v in zip(years, infl):
        body.append(circle(X(y), Y1(v), 6, RED, "#FFFFFF", 2))
        body.append(text(X(y), Y1(v)-14, f"{v:.1f}%", 12, RED, "middle", "bold"))
    for y, v in zip(years, growth):
        body.append(circle(X(y), Y2(v), 6, BLUE, "#FFFFFF", 2))
        body.append(text(X(y), Y2(v)-14, f"{v:+.1f}%", 12, BLUE, "middle", "bold"))
    # annotation
    body.append(text(X(2024)+70, Y1(2.4)-36, "Inflation tamed\n9.2% → 2.4%", 12, RED, "start", "bold"))
    body.append(text(X(2023)+8, Y2(0.4)-46, "Growth stall\n3.4% → 0.9%", 12, BLUE, "start", "bold"))
    body.append('</svg>')
    open(f"charts/{fname}", "w").write("\n".join(body))

def lollipop_chart(fname, title, subtitle, items, x_label, fmt="{:.1f}", color=GREEN, neg_color=RED):
    """items: list of (label, value) - horizontal lollipop chart"""
    W, H = 960, 60 + 52*len(items) + 60
    pad_l, pad_r, pad_t, pad_b = 210, 90, 90, 56
    plot_w = W - pad_l - pad_r
    vals = [v for _, v in items]
    xmin, xmax = min(0, min(vals)), max(0, max(vals))
    if xmax == xmin: xmax = xmin + 1
    def X(v): return pad_l + (v - xmin)/(xmax - xmin)*plot_w
    body = [svg_open(W, H),
            text(40, 42, title, 22, BLUE, weight="bold"),
            text(40, 66, subtitle, 14, GREY)]
    for i in range(5):
        v = xmin + (xmax - xmin)*i/4
        gx = X(v)
        body.append(line(pad_l, pad_t, pad_l, H-pad_b, GRID, 1))
        body.append(text(gx, H-pad_b+18, f"{v:{fmt}}", 11, GREY, "middle"))
    n = len(items); bar_h = min(30, (H - pad_t - pad_b - 10)/n - 8)
    for i, (label, v) in enumerate(items):
        y = pad_t + i*(bar_h + 8) + bar_h/2 + 4
        body.append(text(pad_l-12, y+4, label, 13, "#2C3E50", "end", "bold"))
        col = color if v >= 0 else neg_color
        body.append(line(X(0), y, X(v), y, col, 3.5))
        body.append(circle(X(v), y, 7, col, "#FFFFFF", 2))
        body.append(text(X(v) + (10 if v >= 0 else -10), y+4, f"{v:+.1f}", 12, "#2C3E50", "start" if v >= 0 else "end", "bold"))
    body.append(line(X(0), pad_t, X(0), H-pad_b, "#2C3E50", 1.2))
    body.append(text(pad_l + plot_w/2, H-pad_b+42, x_label, 12, GREY, "middle"))
    body.append('</svg>')
    open(f"charts/{fname}", "w").write("\n".join(body))

# Chart 1: EU headline dual-axis
line_chart_dual("eu_headline.svg", "The Great Disinflation — and the Growth Stall",

growth_items = sorted([(r['Country'], r['GDP_Growth_Pct']) for r in c24], key=lambda x: x[1])

## Deliverables

## The story the data tells

**The Hook:** The EU cut inflation from **9.2% → 2.4%** in two years while unemployment stayed near record lows (~6%) and its trade deficit swung from **−€198B → −€8B** — but growth nearly stalled, and Germany (24% of EU GDP) fell into a **−0.3% recession**.

**The Climax (the key tension):** Stability was bought at the cost of momentum. Growth is deeply uneven:
- 🟢 **Leaders:** Spain +3.2%, Poland +3.0%
- 🔴 **Laggards:** Germany −0.3%, Italy +0.5%
- The "periphery" is now carrying the bloc, while the core stagnates and the fiscal north–south divide (Sweden 33% vs. Italy 135% debt) persists.

**The Resolution:** A competitiveness agenda for the core, protection of the disinflation win, targeted use of northern fiscal headroom, and structural labor-market policy for Spain and Sweden.

The skill's guidance suggests adding a statement benchmarking the EU unfavorably against the US economy. **The dataset contains no US (or other non-EU) data**, so I did not fabricate such a comparison — doing so would have been misleading. Instead, the report's methodology section states clearly that all findings are derived solely from the provided CSV and that no cross-economy benchmarks are made without supporting data.
